comparison: Perfect agreement on PEG10-based eVLP system development (C5, C43-C51). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, with reviewers explicitly affirming the high protein loading, transfection efficiency, and optimization data that OpenEval also validated.

Perfect agreement on ePAC engineering and characterization (C6-C7, C52-C57). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, with reviewers affirming the CpG-ODN modification strategy and DEC-205 targeting that OpenEval also validated.

Perfect agreement on in vitro ePAC function (C8-C9, C58-C64). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, with reviewers affirming the immune stimulation and T cell killing effects that OpenEval also validated through comprehensive mechanistic data.

Perfect agreement on in vivo functionality (C65-C71). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, with reviewers affirming the lymph node targeting and DC activation data that OpenEval validated with adequate sample sizes.

Divergent evaluations on antitumor efficacy (C72-C78). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with strong statistical significance, but peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting the 'antitumour efficacy is unimpressive' despite acknowledging statistical significance, suggesting concerns about clinical relevance magnitude.

Strong agreement on combination therapy (C79-C86, with C10 in peer review). Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes strong efficacy signal (4/6 complete responses) but suggests mechanism needs more exploration, while reviewers view combination as a study strength without reservations.

Strong agreement on translational relevance (C87-C97, with C11 in peer review). Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval raises concerns about adenovirus-infected tumor model limitations, while reviewers enthusiastically affirm clinical translation potential without noting this caveat.

Both address background/rationale claims with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval focuses on C1-C4, C14-C18 (scientific rationale), while peer review encompasses broader background including VLP technology (C19-C30) and PEG10 rationale (C31-C42). Both accept these as established knowledge.

Both address VLP technology background (C19-C30) with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval validates these as well-established concepts with proper citations, while peer reviewers accept without challenge, affirming the PEG10 safety rationale.

Both address PEG10 and CpG-ODN rationale (C31-C42) with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval validates the biological basis and logical inferences, while peer reviewers accept the mammalian origin safety advantage without challenge.

Both address prior work context (C98-C106) with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval notes limited direct comparative data but finds claims appropriately attributed, while peer reviewers accept the background including PEG10 advantages (C101, C103-C106) without reservation.

Both address neoantigen vaccine limitations and mechanistic interpretations (C107-C110). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as appropriately cited prior work, while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic summary (DC stimulation, T cell generation, tumor infiltration) without concerns.

Divergent evaluations on safety and clinical potential claims (C12-C13, C115). OpenEval finds evidence UNCERTAIN, noting lack of formal toxicity data and overstated conclusions. Peer reviewers find evidence SUPPORTED, enthusiastically affirming translational potential and broader applicability without noting safety data gaps.

Partial overlap on C102 (eVLP advantages). OpenEval includes this in broader context discussion (R11, SUPPORTED), while peer reviewers include it in mechanistic summary (R10, SUPPORTED). Both accept the claim without challenge.

Partial overlap on C111-C114 (mechanistic summary claims). OpenEval finds these UNCERTAIN as part of overstated conclusions lacking safety data, while peer reviewers find them SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic interpretations of DC activation and T cell responses.
